title: Explain: opposite pointers
content_md: Read the function and explain what it returns, why the pointers move, and the complexity.
expected_points: Sorted array, find if two values sum to target.
Move the pointer on the side that makes the sum too big or too small.
O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
Fails if the array is not sorted.

title: Explain: half the range
content_md: Explain the loop, the return value, and what happens when the value is missing.
expected_points: Finds target in a sorted array.
Each step discards half the range.
O(log n) time.
Returns -1 when lo passes hi.

title: Explain: depth-first count
content_md: Explain what the nested function counts and why `seen` is needed.
expected_points: Counts nodes reachable from start in an undirected graph.
seen prevents infinite recursion on cycles.
O(V + E) time.

title: Explain: top k
content_md: Explain which values stay in the heap and the complexity.
expected_points: Returns the k largest values, not sorted.
Min-heap of size k.
O(n log k) time.

title: Explain: shrinking window
content_md: Explain what the function returns and when `left` moves.
expected_points: Longest substring without a repeated character.
left jumps past the previous copy of the current character.
O(n) time with a map of last indexes.

title: Explain: union by parent
expected_points: Disjoint-set with path compression.
unite returns false when both nodes were already connected.
Nearly O(1) per operation.

title: Explain: one-row recurrence
content_md: Explain the meaning of `best[i]` and why the loop walks backward.
expected_points: 0/1 knapsack: max value with capacity cap.
best[w] is the best value using capacity w.
Backward loop so each item is used once.
O(n * cap) time, O(cap) space.

title: Explain: prefix tree
content_md: Explain what `add` stores and what `has_prefix` answers.
expected_points: Each edge is one character.
end marks a complete word.
has_prefix is true for a prefix even if that prefix is not a stored word.
Lookup is O(length).
